Hi team —

I ran a short, deal-specific model using our internal bench and the workload assumptions from Sarah. Summary (attaching latency_benchmark_09052026.csv with raw runs):

Assumptions used: average gen 160 tokens, 1.2 calls/session, warm KV cache for retrieval on 40% of calls, batching enabled with adaptive micro-batching tuned to 20ms target.

Measured throughput per GPU (approx, steady-state, 95th percentile machine numbers):
- redwood-13B-q4k (H100 equivalent): ~3,400 tokens/sec per GPU (with batching + cache benefits) at p95 latency ~180ms.
- redwood-70B-q8 (H100 equivalent): ~1,700 tokens/sec per GPU at p95 latency ~320ms.

Modeling notes and mapping for Spectra targets (8k sustained, 12k short spike):
- Primary plan (cost-conscious, meets p95 < 250ms): use redwood-13B-q4k as main model. To achieve 8k sustained, we need ~8,000 / 3,400 = 2.35 -> round up to 3 GPUs in steady-state.
- For 12k spikes (3-minute bursts), we recommend either autoscale burst (if using Dedicated burst pool) or keep a hot spare: 12,000 / 3,400 = 3.53 -> 4 GPUs to cover spike without dropping below p95 target.
- Fallback/fallback-quality plan: keep a small 70B cluster for high-quality requests that exceed a complexity threshold. To handle expected fallback volume (we estimated 10% of calls), 10% of 8k = 800 tokens/sec -> 800 / 1,700 = 0.47 -> 1 GPU for 70B for baseline.

Recommended committed slab and headroom (12-month):
- Baseline commit: 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs (covers 8k sustained + short 12k spikes with ~15% ops buffer). This is the minimum we recommend for a predictable SLA and to avoid immediate autoscale for normal spikes.
- Ops headroom: add 1 additional GPU (total 5) for maintenance, upgrades, and unexpected load (roughly 25% headroom). Commit 5 GPUs if you want >99% confidence in staying within p95 targets without relying on burst pool.
- Alternative cost-optimized commit: commit 3 GPUs + autoscale burst to 5 for peak minutes (saves commit cost but adds complexity).

Latency fit:
- With 4 committed GPUs serving 13B, modeled p95 is ~200ms (measured). p99 will be closer to 700–900ms during small microburst windows unless burst pool is available.
- If Spectra requires hard p99 < 1s, recommend the 5-GPU commit.

PoC (4-week) recommendation:
- Short 4-week PoC: provision 3 committed GPUs (13B) + 1 burst-capable GPU for spikes and 1 small 70B instance for validation. This is minimal to validate integrations and realistic latency behavior without a full-month commitment.

Operational notes / suggestions:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for retrieval-heavy flows to reduce token generation and improve effective tokens/sec. We observed ~12–18% effective tokens/sec uplift with caching on our runs.
- Consider quantization profile q4k for 13B to maximize throughput; q8 remains our standard for 70B fallback to preserve quality.
- Autoscaling policy suggestion: keep a cold-to-warm ramp of 60–90s for new GPUs; prefer hot spares for business-hour high spikes.

I attached the CSV with run details and the short cost sketch. Happy to run a few sample prompt classes from Spectra if you can share a small corpus — that will tighten the numbers.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Latency & Bench Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: latency_benchmark_09052026.csv (CSV with per-GPU runs and micro-batch settings)
